guard.note: FTB Chunks 2101.1.23: modified-chunk list under the manager lock, an early return when empty, copies of the five arrays, then the map-thread task below through FTBChunksClient.MAP_EXECUTOR

the map-thread task: five fresh 512 x 512 BufferedImages (type 2 = TYPE_INT_ARGB data, type 1 = TYPE_INT_RGB foliage / grass / water / blocks), one setRGB each per pixel in the order the redirect ordinals 0-4 name, then writeData of Map.of(name -> image)
the images are only PNG-encoded into the region zip (ImageIO.write), never drawn

ftbchunks_region_write_direct.conversion: @Redirect of each of the five BufferedImage.setRGB(III) calls in MapRegionData.write()'s map-thread task (lambda$write$0) to a handler per call site that stores the pixel into the image's DataBufferInt array (rgb for TYPE_INT_ARGB, rgb & 0xFFFFFF for TYPE_INT_RGB) after a once-per-image layout check (helper bons.furious.patch.ftbchunks_c49.RegionWriteDirect)
ftbchunks_region_write_direct.license: FTB Chunks is All Rights Reserved: none of its code is carried; the redirects store into the JDK image's own array

guard.note: MAP_EXECUTOR.execute(task): hands the task to the map thread
collects changed block positions per chunk for the re-render tasks
the collected positions become ChunkUpdateTasks through queueOrExecute
every received chunk becomes a ChunkUpdateTask through queueOrExecute (claims do not pass here)

ftbchunks_map_writing_off.conversion: cancellable @Inject at the HEAD of FTBChunksClient.queueOrExecute(MapTask) and FTBChunksClient.rerender(BlockPos): with the switch on both return at once (helper bons.furious.patch.ftbchunks_c49.MapWritingOff)
ftbchunks_map_writing_off.license: FTB Chunks is All Rights Reserved: none of its code is carried; the injects only return early
